summary.text: Paula Hicks-Hudson is a Democratic state senator from Ohio who has represented District 11 since January 2023 and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026.
An attorney, she previously served as Toledo's mayor and in the Ohio House.

paragraphs.text: Paula Hicks-Hudson is from Hamilton, Ohio.

She received a bachelor's degree in political science and journalism from Spelman College in 1973, a master's degree in communications development from Colorado State University in 1975, and a J.D. from the University of Iowa.
She has worked as an attorney for the Toledo Legal Aid Society, an assistant prosecutor for Lucas County and an assistant public defender.
Hicks-Hudson was appointed to the Toledo City Council in January 2011 to fill the District 4 seat vacated by Michael Ashford.
The council appointed her mayor of Toledo in 2015, and she lost a re-election bid in the November 2017 general election, according to Ballotpedia.
She then served in the Ohio House of Representatives from 2019 to 2022, representing District 44.
She took office in the Ohio Senate on January 1, 2023, succeeding Teresa Fedor, and in 2023–2024 was assigned to committees including Finance, Judiciary, and Energy and Public Utilities.
Hicks-Hudson advanced from the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary and faces Republican James Nowak and Libertarian Kenneth Sharp in the general election.
